newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products mixed, fuel oil falls sharply.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products mixed, fuel oil falls sharply.

text.p: Med oil products were mixed on Thursday with gasoline and gas oil firmer but naphtha weak and a fuel oil prices falling.
Naphtha remained depressed but firm Far East markets and limited offers of product after the recent arbitrage offtake were seen braking further falls.
Traders said perceptions of strengthening gasoline prices for the spring season were lending the forward market a firmer undertone.
Ras Lanuf barrels were heard offered at around $189 with April paper holding a steady premium of around $5 a tonne.
Gasoline prices remained firm in tight supply. Eurograde cargoes valued around $217 cif Med.

Gas oil strengthened on the back of firmer futures and increased demand. Black Sea Russian gas oil has been moving eastwards, primarily to India, but also to Singapore. There was interest for a 60,000 tonne cargo out of Constanta which remained uncovered. The Brazilian demand from the Med has eased a touch, but was giving some support.
Russian cargoes were assessed at cif high quotes +$2.50 basis Genoa, while non Russian 0.2 percent was pegged around fob high +$3.
A Saras 1.0 percent cargo sold at fob high quotes +$1.50 loading second half March.
Diesel premiums were put at around cif high EN590 quotes -50 to -$1.50.
High sulphur fuel oil prices fell sharply on the back of a sale to a Spanish refiner of some prompt Turkish material at $85.50 cif Las Palmas. A deal earlier in the week was done at $90 cif.
"This fall has been building for a while," said one trader. "Some players were trying to hold the market up so this has been waiting to happen."
